News.title: UK beauty chain returns to high street and opens 6 new stores after going into administration
News.content:
UK beauty chain returns to high street and opens 6 new stores after going into administration

The discount health and beauty retailer is making its return with a new store concept

View 2 Images UK beauty chain returns to high street after going into administration

Budget health and beauty chain Bodycare is staging a major high street comeback, revealing plans to launch six new shops just months after going bust. The retailer, which closed all 147 of its stores in 2025, has now secured premises at prime shopping centres nationwide.

‌



The new branches will open at Merry Hill in Dudley, Derbion in Derby, The Moor in Sheffield, Highcross in Leicester, The Mall in Blackburn and St Johns in Leeds, representing the brand's first physical stores since being rescued from collapse.

‌



Established in 1970, Bodycare started life as a modest British chain specialising in budget toiletries and basic beauty products. Throughout subsequent decades, it expanded gradually into a recognisable high street fixture establishing itself as a go-to destination for competitively priced branded health and beauty items.

‌



View 2 Images The beauty chain was acquired out of administration in October 2025 (Image: kirkgate Shopping Centre)

Yet like numerous retailers, Bodycare encountered mounting pressures in recent times. Escalating operational expenses, evolving shopping patterns and the relentless expansion of e-commerce placed strain on its shop network. These struggles eventually forced the company into administration in 2025 triggering the shutdown of its entire estate.

Bodycare was bought out of administration in October 2025 by an investment consortium headed by Charles Denton, former chief executive of Molton Brown and The Body Shop. Bodycare is rolling out a brand new concept across its latest stores. According to sole adviser Newmark, the new outlets will launch under a fresh 'Bodycare Studio' format, featuring in-store demonstration zones, display screens, live broadcast studios and dedicated creator spaces.

‌



The six locations were selected on the basis of their strong trading history prior to the retailer's collapse. The company is now targeting a further 19 store openings before the end of 2026, with an ambitious long-term goal of establishing more than 200 sites across the country, reports the Express.

New Bodycare stores opening in 2026

Merry Hill in Dudley

Derbion in Derby

The Moor in Sheffield

Highcross in Leicester

The Mall in Blackburn

St Johns in Leeds

David Stern, managing director at Bodycare, said: "Since the acquisition of Bodycare, the team has reimagined both the in-store experience and the brand's digital presence.

Article continues below

"The response from the industry to date has reinforced our confidence to scale quickly and we are looking forward to welcoming customers back as soon as possible. Newmark has been instrumental in supporting us in our ambitious vision."

David Purslow, executive managing director at Newmark, said: "Bodycare is executing a compelling retail strategy - moving at pace but with clear direction and a disciplined approach which sets it up for success.

"Our priority is to ensure the property strategy underpins the brand's momentum as it scales nationally."

News.title: High street stores closing in April 2026 — Marks and Spencer, New Look and more
News.content:
High street stores closing in April 2026 — Marks and Spencer, New Look and more

Some of the affected stores are offering a closing-down sale.

View 2 Images Full list of high-street stores closing in April - Marks and Spencer, New Look and more (Image: Getty)

Marks and Spencer is shutting 14 in-store cafés this year as part of a store overhaul aimed at making way for more products. Some of the closures are set to happen in April.

‌



M&S regional manager Katie Whelan said that following a review of certain stores, they are "re-purposing the café space to provide more product choice and improve the shopping experience". She added: "We understand this will be disappointing news for some of our customers; however, our teams will continue working hard to serve them in-store."

‌



M&S cafés currently offer daily deals for shoppers, including a 10% senior discount and a kids' menu for £4.50.

‌



View 2 Images M&S cafes have daily offers for shoppers, including 10% senior discount (Image: Getty)

Fashion chain New Look shut 51 UK stores last year, with one further closure expected this month. The New Look branch in Carrickfergus, Northern Ireland, is currently holding a closing-down sale, with its last trading day on April 15.

‌



New Look stores closing

The Original Factory Shop fell into administration at the start of the year and has since closed dozens of locations.

The retailer has confirmed that its Redruth and Stanley branches are among the April closures. Last month, the company closed its stores in Norfolk, Suffolk, Cromer, Gorleston-on-Sea, Snettisham, Garstang, and Bungay.

News.title: Dark secret world of Roblox - suicides, school shooters and paedophile paradise
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Dark secret world of Roblox - suicides, school shooters and paedophile paradise

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT. As Carlo Tritta is jailed for 28 months after grooming a girl using Roblox, the Mirror takes a look at some of the cases that have escalated concern over the online game

View 12 Images Parents have voiced concerns ovee just how safe Roblox actually is

A 19-year-old who used the gaming platform Roblox to groom a young girl has been jailed for 28 months, sparking fresh shudders among parents.

The sentencing of Carlo Tritta has pulled back the curtain on a series of catastrophic safety failures on the platform, ranging from predatory grooming to the glorification of school shooters.

Tritta, from Eastleigh, began targeting the 14-year-old victim in September 2024. What began as a in-game chat on Roblox escalated into a toxic obsession that saw the teenager travel across the country to the girl's family home to threaten them in person.

Tritta "love-bombed" the teenager with gifts, phone calls and "highly sexualised' messages on platforms such as Snapchat, Discord and WhatsApp, making her believe that they were in a relationship.

After the girl's mother discovered intimate images and videos, she reported him to police. In August 2025, Tritta was arrested and subsequently bailed under strict conditions not to contact the girl or her mum, all while officers investigated the contents of his seized phone.

View 12 Images Tritta visited the girl's house twice (Image: Copyright remains with handout provider)

However, matters continued to escalate. Obsessed Tritta proceeded to contact the girl’s friends via social media, calling and texting her multiple times, despite being forbidden to do so, and even sending her two cards via Moonpig in an attempt to get her to drop the case. Tritta even went as far as to report the girl’s mother to child services. He also made contact with police, trying to get the investigating officer taken off the case.

Taking things a step further, Tritta travelled to the girl’s home in Manchester on September 5, letting himself inside through the back door. When the girl asked him to leave, he initially did so, before returning 10 minutes later and demanding her new number. She refused to give this to him, but agreed to go to a nearby pub with him, just to get him away from the family home.

View 12 Images He sent cards imploring her to drop the case (Image: Copyright remains with handout provider)

The next morning, while putting the bins out, the girl's mother caught sight of Tritta ducking behind a garage and confronted him. He left before the police were called.

Tritta was subsequently arrested and charged with perverting the course of justice, which he admitted in court, and was handed a 12-month suspended sentence on December 11.

Just three days later, however, he made the journey to Manchester once more, entering the girl's home and confronting both her and her mum, before damaging a CCTV camera.

He was arrested again and later pleaded guilty to three counts of making indecent images of a child, engaging in sexual communications with a child, and causing a child aged 13 to 15 to watch or look at a sexual image. He admitted witness intimidation and criminal damage.

View 12 Images The 19-year-old told his victim that he'd reported her mum to social services (Image: Copyright remains with handout provider)

In a victim impact statement, the girl said she "felt trapped and upset” and was "scared of going downstairs at night” because she thought the defendant would be there.

The mother, who cannot be named for legal reasons, told how she discovered Tritta’s contact with her daughter after the child became depressed, stopped sleeping well and had suicidal thoughts.

The mother said: "I feel like my daughter has been in some kind of abusive, controlling, coercive relationship with somebody who’s a lot older. I don’t feel safe in my own house, I’ve got cameras up, I’ve got to think about safeguarding, I’ve had to change times of school pickup, when I drop off, I just get jumpy in my own house.”

She said of Roblox: "To me, I just thought it’s a child’s game. I did not think for one minute that these older people, paedophiles, are essentially grooming on these games and contacting these children. I try to tell as many people as possible. Watch what your children are playing; they can be dangerous. I thought, my girl, she gets high grades in school, she can be a bit of a moody teenager but she doesn’t go out. I just thought how lucky am I that I’ve got my daughter at home with me and she’s safe, but I’m in my bedroom and she’s in the other and all this is happening to her.”

DC Jodi Bartlett, who investigated the case, said: "Tritta’s behaviour lays bare the terrifying realities of how criminals use the online world to target and harm vulnerable people. Do you truly know who you, or your child, is speaking to online?

Horrifyingly, this isn't the first case involving Roblox that has sparked concern, with previous incidents connected to unimaginable tragedy.

'Innocent' teenager who 'snapped'

View 12 Images 13-year-old Audree Heinee became sucked into the shadowy world of True Crime Community (TCC)

‌



According to mum, Jaimee Seitz, her daughter Audree Heinee had been an ordinary, happy teenager. Then she ended up falling down a dark rabbit hole into the world of online extremist groups, with tragic consequences. On December 2, 2024, Jaimee entered every parent's worst nightmare when 13-year-old Audree, described as her "best friend", died by suicide.

Sadly, there were more shocks to come when, one week later, detectives sat devastated, Jaimee down and told her Audree had become involved in a group called True Crime Community (TCC). Jaimee, from Kentucky, told FOX 12: “It’s a group that glorifies school shooters, romanticises them, obsessed with them, and they feed off of each other."

Glued to her computer in the days that followed, Jaimee learned of how TCC participants are encouraged to either die by suicide, or take the lives of others through school shootings or bombings. It was a mentality she just couldn't square with her "beautiful, happy, seemingly innocent daughter", who'd loved to dance, draw and make others laugh. She feels as though "something snapped" within Audree before her tragic death.

‌



Wanting to understand, Jaimee read Audree's diary, where she learned the youngster had first encountered TCC members via Roblox, before following them to Discord and TikTok. The diary entries felt a world away from the girl Jaimee had known, a girl she says wouldn't have harmed a living soul. According to Jaimee, who is now suing Roblox: "I never want Audree to be seen that way, or in that light, because that's not who she was. She took her own life because of being groomed and being told she had to."

School shooter horror

12 View 12 Images School shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar used Roblox to create a grotesque simulator (Image: Facebook) 12 View 12 Images The 18-year-old killed eight people during their blood-soaked rampage (Image: Royal Canadian Mounted Police/AF)

‌



On Wednesday, February 11, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar committed one of the worst school shooting atrocities in Canadian history. It later emerged that they'd used Roblox to plan for the chilling attack, which left eight people dead. The twisted teenager, who had previously set fire to their family home in a bid to kill their own parents, brutally killed their 11-year-old stepbrother and 39-year-old mum, Jennifer Strang, before continuing their rampage at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia.

Here, they slaughtered five students and a teacher, while injuring a further 25 people. Van Rootselaar, who identified as female, then turned the gun on themselves, dying by a self-inflicted gunshot. As detectives worked to establish a motive behind such a diabolical crime, it emerged that Van Rootselaar had previously used Roblox to create a mass shooting simulator, set against the backdrop of a virtual shopping mall.

View 12 Images The platform - which allows users to create and play 3D games - is now facing lawsuits from grieving parents

‌



As reported by 404 Media at the time, users of this simulator could pick up weapons, in the guise of their Roblox avatars, and shoot at each other. When approached by The Guardian about this revelation, Roblox issued the following statement: “We have removed the user account connected to this horrifying incident, as well as any content associated with the suspect. We are committed to fully supporting law enforcement in their investigation.”

The company said that the "Mall experience” was only accessible through Roblox Studio, a separate app used by developers for building games, with this particular simulator recording just seven visits. Roblox added that it uses both AI and a team of safety specialists to review any uploaded content before it is shown to other users.

Sick Jeffrey Epstein content

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Earlier this year, TMZ reported that a Roblox user had created an in-game version of Little Saint James, Jeffrey Epstein's notorious island, where the convicted sex offender allegedly trafficked his victims. The so-called "Saint Silverlemon Isle" includes several cabanas, a yacht, a secret underground temple, and a villa with a massage table. According to the game description, players must "survive Jeffery the Killer and Donald on the island", making reference to the one-time friendship between paedophile Epstein and President Donald Trump.

View 12 Images Roblox is used primarily by children, but has been targeted by predators, lawsuits allege

According to a lawsuit in August 2025, Roblox had more than 900 user profiles registered with variations of Epstein's name, plus hundreds of games themed around Sean "Diddy" Combs, The Mirror US reports. The lawsuit claims "Roblox is fully aware that these experiences pervade its app, and it allows them to continue to exist unchecked despite the ability to control or eliminate them," and it claims that the consequences for kids can be catastrophic.

‌



Groomed by sexual predator

12 View 12 Images Ethan Dallas was targeted by an adult predator pretending to be a child 12 View 12 Images The 'bright, imaginative boy' was just 15 years old when he died by suicide

‌



Remembered as a "bright, imaginative boy", Ethan Dallas began playing Roblox at the age of nine years old, with parental controls in place. Sadly, things took a harrowing turn when the Californian schoolboy was 12 years old, with “an adult sex predator” targeting him on the platform, while pretending to be a child.

According to a lawsuit that has since been filed against Roblox by Ethan's mother, Becca Dallas, back in September, while conversations began innocently enough, things "gradually escalated to sexual topics and explicit exchanges." As previously reported by NBC News, the paedophile eventually persuaded Ethan to turn off parental controls and to chat with him over Discord. It was here that the adult predator "increasingly demanded explicit photographs and videos”, threatening Ethan that he’d share the images if he didn't do what he said. Ethan complied with these instructions out of fear, with the ordeal taking a terrible toll.

View 12 Images Screengrab from body cam footage issued by Hampshire Constabulary of the arrest of Carlo Tritta (Image: PA)

‌



Sadly, on April 3, 2024, Ethan, remembered in his obituary as someone who "brought joy and laughter to all who knew him", died by suicide at the age of just 15 years old. As detailed in the complaint, the teenager, of San Diego County, had been "permanently harmed and haunted" by his experiences of being groomed online.

This lawsuit accuses both Roblox and Discord of wrongful death, fraudulent concealment and misrepresentations, negligent misrepresentation and strict liability, arguing that, had Roblox and Discord taken steps to screen users before allowing them access to apps, or introduced measures such as age and identity verification, “Ethan would have never interacted with this predator, never suffered the harm that he did, and never died by suicide.”

Speaking to the Mirror in light of the recent Carlo Tritta case, mum Becca shared: "Ethan’s case is just one of far too many, and what’s most heartbreaking is that it didn’t have to happen. Companies like Roblox have had the resources and the reach to prioritise children’s safety from the beginning - but instead, it feels like profit has come first.

‌



"There has been a lack of urgency, accountability, and genuine care. It’s hard to understand how a company of that size did not already have stronger protections in place to prevent the kinds of harm we are now seeing - children being exploited, manipulated, and tragically, some losing their lives. Why did it take so many children being harmed for action to even begin? And even now, for many families, it feels like too little, too late."

She continued: "This doesn’t just impact the children - it devastates entire families. When a child is lost, the ripple effects are lifelong. Parents, siblings, loved ones - they carry that pain every single day. Many families struggle with overwhelming grief, guilt, and trauma, questioning what they could have done differently, when the reality is that these platforms should have been safer from the start. Ethan mattered. Every one of these children matters. And their stories deserve to be heard - not just as statistics, but as lives that should have been protected.

"For Ethan, the man who harmed Ethan is not in jail. He is in the mental hospital because he's claiming he's mentally sick, mind you. From what I'm hearing, he had a really strong desire to play this stuff, and that's what's sad. He's never seems like he's not gonna pay for what he's done I want us. It's just like all these families in justice."

‌



A spokesperson from The Cyber Helpline told the Mirror: "Cases like this are deeply concerning, and unfortunately not isolated. Platforms like Roblox are designed to be social and immersive - that's part of their appeal. But those same features are the ones that create opportunities for harm when the proper safeguards are not in place.

"One of the key risks is the ease of initiating contact with minimal friction on platforms, often without needing to be connected as friends. And even when adding someone as a friend is a requirement, young people do not always understand the risks of who they are adding, excited at the opportunity to make a new friend or curious at who they are.

"While there are safety settings in place, for example, features that require parents or carers to approve friends, these are not always fully understood, consistently applied or robust enough. Ultimately, the onus is, far too often, on parents, carers and young people themselves to turn on safety settings. This is not good enough, and platforms should commit to turning on safety settings by default.

‌



"There are also challenges around moderation and enforcement of platform policies. Platforms operating at a large scale face difficulties identifying harmful behaviour and safety systems are too often reactive rather than preventative, relying on young people to report, when they may not realise themselves that they are experiencing harmful behaviour. We need platforms to become safer by design, with improved detection of grooming and harmful behaviours, clearer and more accessible reporting and help tools, and greater transparency from platforms about how risks are managed. Ultimately, safeguarding needs to be treated as a must-have, not an optional add-on."

When approached for comment, a Roblox spokesperson told the Mirror: “We are deeply saddened to hear of this troubling case. Criminal behaviour has no place on Roblox. Since January, Roblox has required all users to go through age checks in order to communicate on our platform, with the system designed to limit communications to people of similar ages and those they already know. Our policies firmly prohibit any kind of child exploitation, and we have extensive safety systems in place to help prevent user-to-user image sharing and limit chat for younger users, with our teams working closely with law enforcement to support investigations.

"While no system is perfect, we continue to evolve and strengthen our protections every day. For example, last year we added advanced AI systems designed to detect and prevent grooming and stricter chat protections that block personal information sharing and attempts to move conversations off-platform, where moderation standards may be less stringent.”

Article continues below

For emotional support, you can call the Samaritans 24-hour helpline on 116 123, email jo@samaritans.org, visit a Samaritans branch in person or go to the Samaritans website.

Do you have a story to share? Email me at julia.banim@reachplc.com

News.title: TV magician Paul Daniels' nephew stuns BGT judges 10 years since uncle's cancer death
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: TV magician Paul Daniels' nephew stuns BGT judges 10 years since uncle's cancer death

Magician James Phelan will transfix Simon Cowell and co on ITV's Britain's Got Talent tonight, an audition which he hopes will make his late uncle Paul Daniels proud

View 6 Images James Phelan is a magician and nephew of the late Paul Daniels (Image: Tom Dymond)

It’s a magic moment for James Phelan tonight when he conjures up memories of his famous relative on Britain’s Got Talent. An accomplished magician, James, 33, learned at the hands of a master - his uncle, Paul Daniels. Or, more accurately, he learned from old VHS video tapes of The Paul Daniels Magic Show. For, while Paul readily performed tricks at the dinner table, he only taught one to James - a simple colour changing card trick.

‌



James says: “My mum asked him to. He never told me how to do anything else, he’d say, ‘It's in one of those books over there. Read those books and you'll find out how it's done’. He didn't want me to be a tribute act, I suppose. He said, ‘don't be me, be you, because you're the best one of you there is’.”

‌



James’s performance on the ITV talent show, in front of mesmerised judges, shows his uncle gave him good advice. He says: “Simon Cowell is a huge lover of magic and Amanda Holden seemed to like magic before anyone else did. The audition felt like a real moment and it was a way for me to feel close to my uncle Paul again, which I think is really lovely. As I stood on stage at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool - somewhere my uncle had performed so many times, his pictures were on the walls as I walked to the stage. I could feel the weight of the room.

‌



View 6 Images Debbie McGee and Paul Daniels take a break from performing in panto Dick Whittington to pose up with James Phelan and his younger brother Matty

“It was such a whirlwind, such a blur and I was just so nervous. I remember walking off and saying to Ant and Dec, ‘I'm going to go get a pint of gin’, which I thought was funny - I don't even drink gin! They're superstars, aren't they? They're always beautifully warm. It helps calm those nerves.”

Already being hailed as an audition that will go down in BGT history, it is actually James’s second time trying out on the show. His first audition was a decade ago. But it was never shown, as it coincided with the sad death of his uncle Paul, aged 77, on 17 March, 2016, within weeks of being diagnosed with a glioblastoma brain tumour.

‌



James, of Cobham, Surrey, says: “My last conversation with my uncle Paul was about the last time I tried to give it a go [on BGT]. Obviously we couldn't show it, because shortly after filming it he'd got poorly and passed away. It’s been 10 years now, almost to the day, and it feels like now's the time to do it.”

James, who studied economics at Southampton University, quit a successful marketing career in London to pursue magic full time. He takes part in live tours around the country and his latest, The Man Who Was Magic, is heading to Edinburgh Fringe this summer. He says: “Magic was my first love and makes up most of my earliest memories. I caught the bug as a child, and there's not been a day of my life since that I've not thought about it. I learned magic from watching my uncle when it was a rainy Saturday, we’d sit and watch them.”

View 6 Images James Phelan is a mega magician in his own right, following in his famous uncle's footsteps (Image: Michael Wharley)

‌



Paul and Debbie McGee, 67, his assistant and wife of nearly 30 years, starred in The Paul Daniels Magic Show on BBC1 from 1979 to 1994. James says of his aunt and uncle: “I didn't understand they were on a TV show. I just knew that it was my uncle Paul. I always remember when I was seven going to a friend’s house and them having a Paul Daniels magic set and me not understanding why they had my auntie and uncle on their magic set and not their own auntie and uncle!”

He shares another touching memory, saying: “When I was nine, I told my teachers that my uncle Paul was going to come and do a show for us at Christmas for the class… but I hadn't actually asked him. At the school gate, my teacher said, ‘James said that Paul is going to come and do a show for us at Christmas’. And my mum went, ‘did he?!’ We went home and rang him. He was doing panto in Windsor at the time and he took a day off rehearsals and came and did a little show for our school.”

Now James hopes his BGT performance would make Paul proud. He says: “Whether you’re eight or 80, people enjoy magic in the same way. Magic is for all, and it is pure escapism.” Jamie, whose partner Bobbie, 33, is a dancer, says conjuring tricks have been magic for his confidence. He says: “At school there were times I felt invisible, as many children can, and magic helped me to find my place. Then, at uni, I’d never go out without a pack of cards in my pocket.”

‌



And he would love to teach the King - who joined the Magic Circle in 1975 after performing a cups and balls trick - a trick or two. James says: “We do a routine in the show where a child tells us what they want to be when they grow up. We have a coin and it ends up engraved on the coin in his hand. I'd like to know what the King would like to do when he grows up!”

6 View 6 Images James at his Nan’s house, when he was around two years old 6 View 6 Images Paul Daniels and Debbie McGee, pictured in 2015, a year before Paul's death (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



But first, he’d like to win the BGT crown - following in the footsteps of last year’s winner, 24-year-old illusionist Harry Moulding. He says: “There’s always room for more magic. And, right now, we need more magic in the world. You do get detractors that say, ‘not another magic act.’ But magic breeds magic, and the more magic we have the better.”

James remains very close to his Aunt Debbie - who is his mum’s sister - and supported her first stage show since his Uncle Paul’s death this week. She launched a one-woman show in Southampton - reflecting on 50 years in showbusiness - called Debbie McGee Reveals All. James says: “I speak to Debbie every day. She is the most wonderful human being in the world. She’s walked the walk, too. If I ever have any questions about anything to do with the show, I'll ring Debbie and we'll talk through it.”

View 6 Images James wowing the judges on BGT (Image: Tom Dymond)

Article continues below

Clearly extremely proud of James, Debbie, says: “It’s fantastic that my nephew is doing so well in showbusiness. He astounds me with his work ethic, creativity and how natural he is on stage. Full of charisma and love for the audience at such a young age. If his uncle Paul was alive, he would be amazed at what James is achieving. He really is following in Paul’s footsteps.”

*BGT airs on ITV tonight at 6.45pm, and will be available to stream on ITVX

News.title: TAN DHESI: 'Britain can't afford to drift as world gets more dangerous'
News.content:
TAN DHESI: 'Britain can't afford to drift as world gets more dangerous'

'Conflict in the Middle East has spread across the region, causing a humanitarian crisis, and piling pressure on UK Forces already doing more with less', Tan Dhesi, the Defence Committee chair writes

View 2 Images Britain is more exposed than at any point since the Cold War, the chair of the Defence Committee warned (Image: Getty Images)

Britain is more exposed than at any point since the Cold War.

‌



Conflict in the Middle East has spread across the region, causing a humanitarian crisis, straining our partners and piling pressure on UK Forces already doing more with less. As if that wasn’t enough, Moscow has been watching — with Russian submarines tracking the undersea cables that keep our country running. Meanwhile Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has not let up. Ukrainians are fighting every day for their survival.

‌



This is what a more dangerous world looks like — and Britain is not as ready as we should be. The Government hasn’t yet risen to the occasion — and time is not on our side. It needs to start moving much, much faster.

‌



UK is rewriting war response for the first time in 50 years — from rationing to hospitals READ MORE :

OPINION Mikey Smith Donald Trump's weirdest week has left him isolated with nowhere to go on Iran

View 2 Images Britain has not yet risen to the occasion, Tan Dhesi warned (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Last year the Strategic Defence Review set out the long-term vision for our military, but the Defence Investment Plan, or the “DIP”, was meant to provide the details. The Government knows what needs fixing — but the plan to do it, promised for last autumn, is still missing. Months have been lost. In today’s world, that matters.

‌



The lack of a public plan now runs the risk of undermining UK defence, from our vital defence industry to our relationships with partners. For British people, this matters more than Whitehall process. Defence plans guide what kit our forces train with, what equipment is built — from drones and aircraft to tanks and ships — and whether Britain can stand on its own two feet in a crisis.

Without the DIP, we have no plan. No clear direction. No reassurance for our forces or the industry that supports them. Allies want to know not just what Britain says, but what it is prepared to deliver. Uncertainty breeds doubt — and doubt weakens deterrence. And now reports appear to confirm that the Defence Readiness Bill won’t be included in the King’s Speech – another knock for UK defence.

Our nation’s safety is not a party-political issue. My committee is a cross-party group of MPs that holds the Government to account on defence. Members of the committee are seeing the same worrying pattern: deadlines missed, decisions delayed, urgency lacking. Our warnings are based on hard evidence heard in public — from senior military leaders, defence firms, and frontline voices — not party talking points.

‌



For years now we’ve heard that our Armed Forces are “hollowed out” and that we are in a pre-war age. Well, then where is the action? This is too important – we can’t tolerate any further dithering. Whatever is blocking progress in the Ministry of Defence must be cleared — now. Britain cannot afford to drift while the world around us grows more dangerous.

'Give Slough a chance'

Move over Betjeman and Brent, Slough might be the target of punchlines and lazy journo hit pieces, but don’t underestimate this great town Slough’s reputation often precedes it, but its history, culture and technology reach far further than you might think. It’s a huge business and tech hub, delivering for the whole country. It has the second largest concentration of data centres in the world, highest GVA per head in the UK and the largest number of UK corporate HQs outside of London, making it an ideal candidate for a Government’s AI Growth Zone. It’s also the people that make Slough. It’s the community spirit, the multicultural and creative melting pot, with over 150 languages spoken and Pinewood and Shinfield Studios just on our doorstep. So forget what you’ve heard – Slough is on the up!

'Sikh war heroes deserve national memorial'

It’s crucial we have a national memorial.

This project will undoubtedly achieve more incredible milestones and allow us fresh insights into space. Nothing quite shows the endless possibilities of human achievement than space exploration. Welcome home Artemis II!

Nigel Farage losing 'thousands every week' after stopping video messages

Nigel Farage stopped selling filmed messages for £71 each on the Cameo website last month

View 3 Images Nigel Farage on the campaign trail for the local elections (Image: Getty Images)

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is losing around £2,692 a week after halting his lucrative video shout-outs. He stopped selling filmed messages for £71 each on the Cameo website last month. The end came after he allegedly recorded clips for 'questionable' individuals and events. Last November, we revealed the Brexit MP had earned £140,000 from selling personal messages on the US-based platform Cameo in the previous 11 months.

‌



His speaking records showed he had stood up in Parliament on only 22 occasions over the same period - speaking about grooming gangs, Ukraine and migrant boat crossings. But he mentioned his constituents in Essex only three times.

‌



View 3 Images Nigel Farage has a pint in Kent this week (Image: Zeynep Demir Aslim/Zuma Press/eyevine)

‌



Amazon set to discontinue two million Kindles - full list of models READ MORE :

Brooks Koepka read the riot act and called out by coach for breaking agreement READ MORE :

His Cameo page this week stated that 10,700 people were waiting for him to resume creating content. His listing adds: “Nigel Farage is unavailable. Tap to let them know you're waiting and to get notified when they're back." When users ask for details of a potential return, they must log their email. The site adds: "Nigel Farage's Cameo videos offer fans a unique opportunity to receive personalised messages from the former UK politician and Brexit leader. Customers can request messages for a variety of occasions, from birthdays and retirements to roasts and motivational pep talks. "Nigel is often asked to reference his political views on Brexit, immigration, and the Reform UK party, as well as mention specific TV shows, sports teams, and even silly inside jokes. His videos offer fans an entertaining and lighthearted way to connect with his signature straight-talking, anti-establishment style.”

View 3 Images Nigel Farage has suspended his contributions to Cameo video platform (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Farage pocketed £27,800 after flying to the US earlier last month to address an anti-climate think tank with close ties to Donald Trump. Since his election, he has received almost £1.4m in payments from outside interests.

He had hoped to meet President Trump at his Mar-a-Lago complex in Florida to lobby the Trump administration during the week when the U.S. president’s relations with Keir Starmer hit rock bottom over the Iran war.

The meeting didn’t take place, but he still received a large payment. Farage spoke at Club for Growth. It is a conservative anti-tax lobby group based in Washington, D.C. It has vowed “to work closely with President Trump and his team."

Article continues below

Farage stopped using the personalised video platform Cameo after the investigation into more than 4,300 clips. He had recorded them after joining the platform in April 2021.

“I will decline to comment on that,” he said when asked if he would continue to make Cameo videos. “I don't approve of things being published in national newspapers that have been illegally obtained.”

The Guardian denied that any of the information had been illegally obtained. Reform UK was approached for a comment

News.title: BBC Naga Munchetty shares 'best' sentence to say at GP appointment 'to be heard'
News.content:
BBC Naga Munchetty shares 'best' sentence to say at GP appointment 'to be heard'

BBC Breakfast presenter Naga Munchetty has shared advice on speaking to GPs after her own experience

View Image The BBC star's book 'It's Probably Nothing' focuses on women's health (Image: Getty )

Naga Munchetty has revealed what she considers the 'best' sentence to use when visiting your GP to ensure you're properly 'heard'. The BBC Breakfast host has been candid about her own health struggles and her adenomyosis diagnosis, which wasn't confirmed until she was 47, despite experiencing symptoms since her teens.

‌



Five years ago, she detailed her experience of having a coil fitted and discussed her struggles with debilitating, painful periods. The reaction from listeners was extraordinary and prompted her to speak more openly about her symptoms and investigate other women's experiences with medical treatment.

‌



The 51-year-old has penned a book, 'It's Probably Nothing: Critical Conversations on the Women's Health Crisis'. During a previous BBC Radio 4 show, she explained to host Anita Rani why she felt driven to tackle this subject after feeling ignored when seeking medical assistance.

‌



Discussing her book at the time, she told listeners: "I'm sick of women not being listened to." She also offered her guidance on how to speak up and be heard when seeking medical help.

During the Woman's Hour episode, she referenced a section in her book centred around GP appointments. She said: "There's a chapter in here, which I was really nervous about writing, called 'The GP Appointment', because I thought 'this is going to sound really patronising, everyone knows how to book a GP appointment'.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"But, this is more about what you say. You make a list, write down your concerns, you prepare." She explained: "The best sentence I found is, 'this is negatively impacting the quality of my life'.

"You cannot ignore that. 'I have had to take time off work, I am losing my job, I have been unable to care for my children.' You have to be specific, and they must offer you help."

She added: "They want to. This isn't about GPs not wanting to help. This has just got to be a better partnership, so that you are listened to."

‌



Munchetty has battled adenomyosis since her teenage years, and has spoken openly about how deeply frustrating the road to diagnosis was, with doctors repeatedly dismissing her symptoms as 'normal' or advising her to simply push through the pain for years on end.

The BBC presenter endured debilitating symptoms including heavy menstrual bleeding, excruciating pain, and nausea, ultimately turning to private healthcare to seek proper treatment. She has since used her public profile to shine a light on adenomyosis and the struggles women face in accessing appropriate medical support.

‌



She told listeners: "My periods basically involved flooding, which meant that I would also have to set an alarm through the night to change my period products. I'd sleep on a towel, I was in so much pain that I would sometimes sleep on the floor so that it would be painful that way, so I wouldn't have to think about the other pain.

"I would pass out, I would vomit, I would have diarrhoea, and I would still be going to work. I would wear two pairs of knickers and I would always pack a spare pair of tights, I'd never wear white on my bottom half. And, you know, I am not uncommon. And just because it's not uncommon doesn't mean it is normal."

Reflecting on her experiences with medical professionals, she said: "But no one ever asked me or investigated why they are so heavy. I was told, 'you'll grow out of it', what nonsense. 'It'll be better when you have a baby', so I've got to have a baby to stop being in pain?

‌



"And then when it was finally diagnosed, everyone says, 'weren't you relieved?' Yeah, I can put a name to it, but there is no cure. You look into it, and there's not enough research or money put into women's reproductive issues."

What is adenomyosis?

According to the NHS, adenomyosis is a condition where the lining of the womb starts growing into the muscular wall of the uterus. Several treatments are available to help manage symptoms. The condition is most commonly diagnosed in women aged over 30 and can impact anyone who has periods.

‌



While some people may show no symptoms at all, typical indicators of adenomyosis include extremely painful periods and excessive menstrual bleeding. Additional symptoms can manifest at any stage of the menstrual cycle, including pelvic discomfort, abdominal bloating or a sensation of pressure in the tummy, and pain during sex.

It's crucial to understand that endometriosis is a distinct condition where tissue resembling the womb lining develops in other locations, such as the ovaries or fallopian tubes. If you're experiencing severe pelvic or period pain that's worse than normal and doesn't ease with painkillers, book an urgent appointment with your GP or ring NHS 111 for help.

What happens at a GP appointment?

If you're showing symptoms of adenomyosis, your GP may ask about your menstrual cycles. They might also check your tummy for any signs of swelling or bloating. When booking your appointment, don't hesitate to request a female doctor. The doctor may also suggest an internal examination to check your vagina and cervix, which is the passage between the vagina and the uterus.

‌



If you'd like, you can have a friend, relative, or another member of staff present during the examination. In some cases, further tests may be needed to identify the cause of your symptoms or to rule out similar conditions, such as endometriosis. These tests might include an ultrasound or an MRI scan.

What are the treatments for adenomyosis?

If you've been diagnosed with adenomyosis, there are a number of treatment options available to help ease your symptoms. These include:

The IUS (intrauterine system, also known as Mirena or hormonal coil), which helps to thin the lining of the womb, resulting in lighter and less painful periods.

Various forms of hormonal contraception, if the IUS isn't suitable for you, such as the progestogen-only pill, the combined pill, or the contraceptive patch.

Medications like tranexamic acid or NSAIDs.

Article continues below

Should these treatments prove ineffective, surgery may be required. This could mean a hysterectomy or a procedure to remove the womb lining (endometrial ablation).

Can you ease the symptoms of adenomyosis?

There are several ways to help manage period pain or pelvic pain brought on by adenomyosis, including placing a heat pad or hot water bottle wrapped in a tea towel on your stomach. You might also consider using a TENS machine – a small device that delivers mild electrical impulses to relieve pain – or taking over-the-counter painkillers such as paracetamol or ibuprofen.

The NHS says: "It's not clear what causes adenomyosis. You may be more likely to get it if you are over the age of 30 and have given birth."

News.title: Sudanese national charged after four migrants die in English Channel crossing attempt
News.content:
Sudanese national charged after four migrants die in English Channel crossing attempt

Four people, two men and two women, died after trying to cross the English Channel in a small boat which sunk off the coast of Calais

View 2 Images French emergency services at Plage Sud d'Equihen in France, after two men and two women died trying to cross the English Channel (Image: PA)

A man has been charged with endangering life after four migrants tragically died trying to board a small boat crossing the English Channel on Thursday, the National Crime Agency said.

Sudanese national, Alnour Mohamed Ali, 27, is alleged to have piloted the boat from France in a bid to get to the UK.

Two men and two women died as they attempted to climb on to a so-called "taxi boat" - another term for a dinghy - at Equihen-Plage, near Boulogne-sur-Mer, on Thursday morning.

Thirty-eight people were returned to the French shore after the incident south of Boulogne-sur-Mer near Calais, but 74 migrants travelled on to the UK. The head of the Pas-de-Calais region, Francois-Xavier Lauch, said the four migrants were "far out to sea" off the coast when their bodies were found by authorities.

View 2 Images French police were called to Plage Sud d'Equihen (Image: PA)

"I have to commend the actions of our officers and firefighters who, as you know, are deployed every day to stop these crossings," the prefect said at the time pf the incident.

Speaking of the four people who died, he said: "They were already quite far into the sea. The currents, which can be dangerous here, swept them away. This provisional toll – and I insist that it is provisional – states four deceased: two men, two women.

A UK government spokesperson said at the time of the incident: “We are deeply saddened to hear about the deaths in French waters today.

Article continues below

"Every death in the Channel is a tragedy and a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting vulnerable people for profit. We will continue working relentlessly with the French and our partners overseas to prevent these perilous journeys. The French authorities are leading the response to this incident and we are supporting their investigation."

Ali will appear at Folkestone Magistrates' Court today.

A teenager charged with murdering a 14-year-old boy who was shot dead in south-east London has appeared in court.

Eghosa Ogbebor was killed in Lord Warwick Street, Woolwich. Police had been called to the scene at about 3.40pm on 2 April after reports of a shooting.

On Saturday a 16-year-old boy, of Romford, east London, appeared at Thames Magistrates’ Court where he was remanded into youth detention accommodation before his next appearance at the Old Bailey on Tuesday.

The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was arrested on April 4 and released on bail, police said.

He was rearrested on 9 April and charged with murder the following day, the Metropolitan Police said.

On 4 April, officers arrested a 16-year-old boy and a 19-year-old man in Woolwich on suspicion of murder and a 46-year-old man on suspicion of assisting an offender.

open image in gallery Forensic officers near the scene in Woolwich where 14-year-old Eghosa Ogbebor was shot dead ( PA )

All three were released on bail, the police said.

A 14-year-old boy, 16-year-old boy and 18-year-old man were arrested on 3 April in connection with Eghosa’s death and have been bailed while inquiries continue.

On 10 April, another 16-year-old boy was also arrested on suspicion of murder. He remains in custody.

Eghosa’s family are being supported by specialist officers and the investigation remains ongoing, police said on Friday.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has pledged to increase the British army by 20,000 as she warned that any replacement of Donald Trump in the White House will continue his military policies of moving away from European defence.

In a speech to the London Defence Conference, Ms Badenoch admitted to “dismay” at the language used by President Trump but warned that the idea of European defence without US involvement is “a fairytale”.

It came as she pledged "the largest net increase in British troops under any government since the Second World War" if the Tories return to power with an overall increase of 20,000 to the army.

open image in gallery Kemi Badenoch issued a warning on defence as the governments comes under pressure over the state of the country’s armed forces ( Christine Quarmyne/CCHQ )

Her speech comes amid questions over Keir Starmer’s plans to increase defence spending to 5 per cent and concerns over his government’s failure to provide its Defence Investment Plan details.

It also comes just ahead of King Charles III and Queen Camilla going the US on a state visit at the end of April which many are calling to be cancelled.

Sir Keir has said that Trump’s threats to “wipe out a whole civilisation” with the war on Iran have already been criticised by prime minister Sir Keir Starmer who questioned the president's values.

Ms Badenoch said: “Many people find President Trump’s actions to be an anathema. They find his words unstatesmanlike, they find his treatment of allies to be needlessly provocative.

“I have to say that some of the president’s recent social media posts and comments to the press have dismayed me, too. Maybe his successor will return to more traditional diplomacy.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump’s policy reflects the direction of US policy, Ms Badenoch warned ( AFP via Getty Images )

However, she cautioned against a hope that a change in the White House will see a change in policy.

“If we comfort ourselves with these ideas we will miss the underlying lesson that Trump’s presidency is not the start, but a continuation of a change in US outlook and behaviour.

“For decades, the United States has been complaining... at least privately... that Europe is not pulling its weight on defence.

“And the ‘Special Relationship’ has not always been as special as we liked to think. Ronald Reagan invaded Grenada without consulting us, President Biden did the same when he pulled out of Afghanistan.

“President Trump may be unorthodox in how he talks to us but there are forces at play here that are much larger than his presidency.

“The mirror that he is holding up to Europe and that we are finding it so uncomfortable to look in is showing us that without the United States, we cannot properly defend ourselves. At present, European strategic autonomy is a fairytale.”

She went on: “We must reassert ourselves as a serious power in the world. Show our allies what we bring to the table and show our enemies that we are ready to defend ourselves.

“If we do not... we will have no say in whatever comes next.”

open image in gallery Starmer is facing demands from Trump to secure the strategic shipping route the Strait of Hormuz ( UK MOD Crown copyright )

The Tory leader said that this would mean a reversal of post-Cold Wr policy of shrinking the size of the UK military.

Vowing the largest net increase in the size of the military since the Second World War, she vowed to redirect cash from benefits to defence.

She said: "I have announced that the next Conservative government would reinstate the two-child benefit cap and spend that money on defence.

"That will fund the largest net increase in British troops under any government since the Second World War.

"We will use the money to recruit 6,000 regular soldiers and 14,000 reservists as well as paying for their accommodation and equipment.

"I have said that we will reallocate £17 billion from Government R&D and Ed Miliband's disastrous net-zero projects to create a new sovereign defence fund.

"This fund will invest in British defence start-ups, protecting our supply chains and delivering drone technology right across our armed forces, ensuring our army, navy and air force can fight as war is fought today. It is not yet 3 per cent, but it is a start.

"We will find more savings till we get there."

The alleged pilot of a small boat has been charged after four migrants drowned trying to cross the English Channel.

Sudanese national Alnour Mohamed Ali was charged with endangering life, on Friday, after two men and two women died trying to board a small boat crossing the English Channel on Thursday, the National Crime Agency said.

The 27-year-old is alleged to have piloted the boat from France to the UK.

Two men and two women died as they attempted to climb on to a so-called “taxi boat” at Equihen-Plage, near Boulogne-sur-Mer, on Thursday morning.

Thirty-eight people were returned to the French shore after the incident south of Boulogne-sur-Mer near Calais, but 74 migrants travelled on to the UK.

He will appear at Folkestone Magistrates’ Court on Saturday.

The new “taxi boat” people smuggling tactic, designed to avoid detection by French police, involves dinghies travelling along the coast with just a driver to pre-designated beaches, where migrants enter the water to climb on board.

The 27-year-old is alleged to have piloted the boat from France to the UK. ( Associated Press )

Two children were among those taken to hospital as a precaution after the incident on Thursday, and another person was treated for hypothermia.

Endangering another during a journey by sea to the UK is a new offence introduced as part of border security legislation earlier this year.

In January, Aman Naseri, 18, an Afghan national, was the first person to be charged.

According to the Home Office, the offence is designed to stop more people being crammed into unsafe boats and would apply to those involved in physical aggression and intimidation, as well as anyone who resists rescue.

French government official Francois-Xavier Lauch, the prefect of Pas-de-Calais, told reporters on Thursday the people who died were “already quite far into the sea”, adding: “The currents, which can be dangerous here, swept them away.”

The agency is helping French authorities with their investigation.

It came a day after French emergency services took part in a training exercise to practise dealing with migrants in the water at the same beach where the deaths happened.

More than 5,000 migrants have arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel so far this year, according to Home Office data.

Migrant charities repeated calls for the Government to provide safe and legal ways for asylum seekers to arrive in the UK to prevent more death, and Conservatives accused Labour of being “weak” over tackling crossings.

The Government said it was “deeply saddened” by the deaths.

LeBron James made his 12,000 career assist as he spearheaded the short-handed Los Angeles Lakers to a commanding 101-73 victory over the Phoenix Suns on Friday night.

Clinching home-court advantage for the first round of the playoffs. The 41-year-old superstar posted 28 points, 12 assists, and six rebounds, showing no fatigue on the second night of a back-to-back.

James also recorded his 12,000th career assist, becoming only the fourth NBA player to reach the milestone. At the game's end, James' total sat at 12,010.

This second consecutive win, and 15th in 19 games, sees the Lakers (52-29) poised for the third or fourth seed in the Western Conference.

Despite finishing the regular season without injured stars Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, Los Angeles is one game behind third-placed Denver (53-28) with a game left, holding the tiebreaker. Luke Kennard added 19 points, and Rui Hachimura 13.

The NBA scoring king racked up 14 points in the first quarter, and he added six points and seven assists in the second half while making sure the Lakers' lead stayed firm.

The Lakers recovered to lead 57-48 at halftime. James had 22 points and Kennard added 17 in the half.

open image in gallery LeBron James scored 28 points and dished 12 assists to become the fourth player in NBA history to top 12,000 in a career, leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a convincing 101-73 victory over the visiting Phoenix Suns ( AP )

Late in the third quarter, James scored on a layup to push the lead to 17. Then he stole the ball and cruised uncontested for a ferocious dunk that made it 79-60 with 1:12 left in the period.

Los Angeles held an 81-64 edge entering the fourth quarter and led by as many as 29 as Phoenix managed just nine final-quarter points on 4-of-21 shooting (19 per cent).

The Suns committed 24 turnovers and shot just 33.8 per cent, including a shaky 7 of 40 (17.5 per cent) from behind the arc.

Dillon Brooks scored 12 points for the Suns, who are seventh in the West standings and locked into the top spot in the play-in tournament.

Devin Booker sat out for Phoenix to rest his injured right ankle for the postseason, and Jalen Green also sat with right knee soreness. Collin Gillespie and Grayson Allen played in the first half, but sat in the second half of the Suns' lowest-scoring performance of the season.

open image in gallery Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James (23) controls the ball against Phoenix Suns guard Koby Brea (14) ( IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect )

The Lakers' injury woes remain dire, but Marcus Smart had six points and seven assists against Phoenix in his return from a nine-game injury absence.

James scored or assisted on nine of the Lakers' first 10 field goals while they streaked to an early 16-point lead.

Susan Sarandon was among the famous names enlisted by Sabrina Carpenter for her showstopping Coachella set in the desert.

The 26-year-old pop star was the first headliner of this year’s California music festival, performing on Friday night (10 April).

Her Old Hollywood-themed performance transformed the stage into “Sabrinawood”, and featured surprise cameos from stars including Sarandon, Will Ferrell, Corey Fogelmanis, and Landman actor Sam Elliott.

Sarandon, in particular, was a stand-out. The 77-year-old actor delivered a nearly seven minute-long dramatic monologue in the middle of Carpenter’s set in which she played an older version of the singer.

Dressed in a crisp white shirt in a classic car, the actor reflected on “what it was like to be a star” in her prime – and ruminated on what a future niece would think of her.

Fans on social media have reacted to the moment, calling Sarandon and Carpenter an “iconic” duo.

Elsewhere, however, Variety reported that the elongated scene – also featuring Carpenter’s Girl Meets World co-star Corey Fogelmanis as a waiter at a drive-in theatre – “brought the pop show to a screeching halt” with “lots of people leaving” as a result.

Sarandon made headlines earlier this year when the actor spoke out during an emotional press conference about being blocked by Hollywood for speaking out and calling for a ceasefire in Gaza – after which she was fired by her agency in 2023.

Anchorman star Will Ferrell also made a surprise appearance on stage as the festival’s grumpy on-call electrician after the power “short-circuited”.

Carpenter opened her Friday night set with a black-and-white short film depicting her singing along to Kool & the Gang’s “Hollywood Swinging” as she drives down a highway at night in a 1950s classic car.

In a scene reminiscent of Alfred Hitchcock’s Psycho, she is pulled over by a suspicious police officer played by Elliott. After getting back on the road, she eventually arrives at a drive-in that is revealed to be the Coachella festival site. Emerging from the car, Carpenter kicked off the show with a rendition of her hit single “House Tour”.

Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber and Karol G are headlining Coachella 2026 ( Getty )

One famous face not to be seen, however, was Madonna who had been rumoured to appear as the chosen celebrity to be “arrested” in what has become a signature moment in Carpenter’s shows. Other stars to have previously featured in the playful segment include Millie Bobby Brown and Nicole Kidman

Taking place across two weekends from Friday (10 April) to Sunday (19 April), this year’s Coachella is headlined by Carpenter, Justin Bieber and Karol G.

The xx, Disclosure, Teddy Swims, Sexyy Red, Katseye, Central Cee, Ethel Cain, the Strokes, Addison Rae, David Byrne, Iggy Pop, and FKA twigs are among the other artists set to perform during North America’s largest music festival.

News.title: Rory McIlroy surges six clear and sets Masters record after stunning display
News.content:
McIlroy sounded without fear about the prospect. “I’ve built up a nice cushion at this point. I guess my mindset is just trying to keep playing well and keeping my foot on the gas,” he said. “Don’t protect it. Go out and play freely, keep swinging. A big part of the lesson from the 2011 Masters to the 2011 US Open was: don’t get protective. Go out there and keep playing, keep trying to make birdies, stay as trusting and as committed as possible.”

McIlroy knows his pursuers well. In fact, he knows Patrick Reed only too well. The divisive American saw off McIlroy in the last pairing in 2018 to don his Green Jacket. And then, three years ago, McIlroy took a little revenge over Reed at the Dubai Desert Classic in an almighty ding dong that involved the American throwing a tee at the Northern Irishman and a feud developing through the media.

It could still be delicious and following his 69, Reed agreed. “It’s one of those golf courses that if you go out and you post a low number, you just never know,” he said. “That’s the thing about this course, when it starts playing this firm and fast. just have to wait and see what the weekend entails. At the same time I love the position I put myself in. Hopefully I can go out and have a good day tomorrow and have a good shot going into Sunday.”

One shot back of second is McIlroy’s Ryder Cup partner Tommy Fleetwood. The Englishman conjured two eagles in his 68 and with only two blemishes on his card – on the first and last – he will be relishing the challenge of going two better here than two years ago and one better than his two runner-up finishes in the majors.

News.title: I wanted to switch my broadband provider. I had no idea what I was letting myself in for
News.content:
The email was offering me an upgrade to ‘Full Fibre 100’, with speeds of up to 100Mbps for the same price. This package was costing me £53.50 a month, and if you think that sounds expensive, you would be correct.

A quick browse on rival Virgin Media’s website revealed that I could get Gigabit speeds, ten times as fast as what Sky was offering me, for £30.99 per month – increasing to £35.99 next year.

I’m a writer, not a mathematician, but it doesn’t take a genius to figure out that Sky’s £53.50 for 67Mbps (or 100Mbps if I upgraded) was a worse deal than Virgin’s £30.99 for ten times the speed.

In Sky’s defence, every broadband and mobile provider is guilty of this ‘loyalty penalty’. While there are consumer protections in the UK for home and car insurance, preventing companies from offering better deals to new customers than existing ones, this doesn’t apply to broadband or mobile networks.

I’ll also say that I received an email from Sky prior to them telling me about the speed boost, which said I was going to be out of contract soon. So the company did at least try to warn me.

A warning to all – expect a lot of calls

News.title: Trump’s war in Iran sends US petrol prices soaring
News.content:
US petrol prices have soared by more than 20pc in the wake of Donald Trump’s war in Iran.

Energy costs surged by 10.9pc in March, according to the US labour department. That included a 21.2pc monthly rise in gasoline, or petrol, prices and a 30.7pc increase in fuel oil prices.

Overall inflation hit 3.3pc in March, the highest rate in almost two years. It rose by 0.9pc between February and March, the highest monthly gain since June 2022 during the peak of the post-pandemic inflation crisis.

The increase in energy prices alone accounted for nearly three-quarters of the monthly increase.

The jump is a blow for President Trump, who has vowed to tackle the cost of living crisis and faces mid-term elections in the autumn.

Surging energy costs reflect a jump in oil and gas prices since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February.

While oil prices have fallen since the US-Iran ceasefire was announced, they still remain high compared to pre-war levels. Brent crude stood at $96 per barrel on Friday afternoon.

The price pressures will make the Federal Reserve more wary about cutting interest rates.

There are concerns that higher energy prices will also spill out to other areas of the US economy. Grocery prices fell by 0.2pc in March, but economists are concerned that they could begin to creep up in the months ahead.

The applause mostly came from opposition fans, with the AS Monaco midfielder introduced as a 69th-minute substitute at the 19,904-capacity Stade Jean-Bouin.





Pogba had not played a competitive match since suffering a calf injury last December.

He remains hugely popular across France having led them to the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

Online football fans are also pleased to see the four-time Serie A winner back on the pitch.

One wrote: “Hope he genuinely finds some fitness and form, joy to watch.”

Another said: “That odd occasion where he completely took over matches was an incredible sight.”

A third added: “I was never his biggest fan, but at his peak he was absolutely incredible.

“I think if he wanted he could have been world class at any position because he had such great understanding for pace and space … could deliver a killer ball from nowhere.”

In 2016, Manchester United shelled out a then-world record transfer fee of €105 million (£91.5m) for the 33-year-old.

Sports.title: ‘I want to see it again’ – ‘Angeball’ could make shock Tottenham return as De Zerbi vows to bring back Postecoglou style
Sports.content:
THE Ange Postecoglou era may not be over after all — as Roberto De Zerbi wants to bring back his swashbuckling style at Tottenham.

Big Ange’s two-year spell was a wild ride as Spurs soared initially, playing thrilling football and even going five points clear at the top… before nosediving down the table.





His memorable second season saw him win the Europa League, ending their 17-year trophy drought but finish 17th in the league — which led to the Aussie, 60, being sacked.

De Zerbi takes over a Tottenham team in severe danger of the drop with seven games to go.

His initial focus is on rescuing the team from sliding into the Championship but long term he would love a return to the entertaining, possession-dominating days of Postecoglou.

Former Brighton chief De Zerbi, 46, said: “I want to keep the ball. I want to see again the Tottenham I watched with Postecoglou.

“Because in my second season at Brighton, there was Postecoglou here with a lot of these players and it was one of the best teams in terms of quality of play.

“With Pedro Porro, with [Destiny] Udogie, with [Micky] Van de Ven, with [Cristian] Romero and I would like to see it again.”

Lewis Dunk claimed De Zerbi’s exciting but complicated philosophy had left Brighton’s players “baffled” during the Italian’s first fortnight at the Amex in 2022.

Albion failed to win any of their first five games but then flourished, reaching Europe for the first and only time in their 125-year history.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

De Zerbi has no time to waste at Spurs, given their perilous position.

For all the talk of tactics, he insists the biggest change he must make is to his players’ “mentality”, promising not to confuse the squad with any unnecessarily elaborate instructions at this stage.

His big challenge is to lift the players’ shattered confidence after failing to win a single Premier League game in 2026.

None more so than goalie Antonin Kinsky, set to start his first game since being hauled off by predecessor Igor Tudor on 17 minutes after two howlers against Atletico Madrid.

De Zerbi is still missing regular No 1 Guglielmo Vicario ahead of his first game tomorrow at Sunderland after the keeper’s hernia surgery.



But the Italian said: “I haven’t spoken yet with Kinsky as I think he doesn’t need to speak too much.

“I have confidence. He has to be strong but he is strong enough to show what he can do.

“Not more, not less. I think his qualities are enough to play at Spurs. The players believe in him.

“He has to stay calm and confident. He is playing at Tottenham, so he has to be stronger than the mistakes, and to move on.”

He may not have spoken to Kinsky yet but De Zerbi has held individual talks with most of his squad.



That includes skipper Cristian Romero, who is set to keep the armband — despite the issues he has caused on and off the pitch this season.

They include being banned for seven games for red and yellow cards and sniping at the hierarchy with thinly-veiled social- media digs.

Yet De Zerbi explained: “I have spoken with Cristian. I think Cuti is crucial for us.

“He’s the captain, he is maybe the most important player in our squad.

“Like Richarlison, to achieve our goal, we need the best of Romero.”

De Zerbi begins his rescue mission at the Stadium of Light, before home games against old club Brighton, Leeds and Everton — along with trips to Wolves, Aston Villa and Chelsea.



And the former Marseille manager is bullish on his chances of keeping Tottenham in the Premier League — despite their plight.

Asked what gives him such confidence, he replied: “The qualities of the players.

“The guys know the situation is very difficult but if you watch them against Liverpool and also Atletico Madrid in Madrid, they showed their qualities and they showed sometimes the right spirit.

“We now have to show this for 90 minutes and we have to believe in ourselves.

“The most important part in football is the mental part.



“You are used to speaking too much about the style of play, the tactical disposition, blah, blah, blah.

“But, in the end, the mental part is crucial in every work, especially in football, especially in this moment at Tottenham.”

Meanwhile, De Zerbi claimed he was not surprised by the supporter backlash ahead of his appointment because of his support of Mason Greenwood at Marseille.

Greenwood had charges of alleged rape and assault dropped against him in 2023.

De Zerbi described the England striker as a “good guy” who “paid a heavy price” — comments which prompted three Spurs fan groups to campaign against his hiring.



And the Italian added: “I wasn’t surprised. I was a bit sad and sorry it happened because I’m sorry if somebody took offence.

“This topic is very close to me, I’m very sensitive about this topic, because of the person I am and because I have a daughter.

“I have always been against — always — any type of violence, especially against women.

“But not only violence, even just sexist jokes or other sexist behaviour. I have a daughter and I’m directly affected by it.

“I know who I am, I know the type of person I am, so I wasn’t annoyed by the questions — I’m just sad about them.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Asked if he hoped fans would accept his apology, De Zerbi added: “Yes, also because I’m not going to go back over this topic.

“I spoke about it in my first interview, I spoke about it today and it wouldn’t be right to go back over this topic again.”

Sports.title: ‘There are still things in the air’ – Liam Rosenior reveals whether Enzo Fernandez’s Chelsea exclusion could continue
Sports.content:
DESPITE apologising, Enzo Fernandez will not play any part in Chelsea’s clash against Manchester City on Sunday.

And Liam Rosenior, 41, insisted that there is still work to be done on a “few hurdles” before he makes a ‘clear statement’ on the situation, after Fernandez’s comments about a potential move to Real Madrid.





When asked if those hurdles could see Fernandez miss a massive home tie against Man Utd, the Chelsea boss said: “Not in this moment.”

He continued: “He won’t play on Sunday, but hopefully after that, he’ll be a massive part of the group moving forward.

“There are still a few hurdles that need to be overcome that I won’t go into, but at the same time, I want every player really, really focused now on a huge run.

“There are still things in the air that I won’t speak about now. I have a very good relationship with Enzo, as all of us do, but there are still things that need to be cleared before I make a clear statement on the situation.”



Fernandez, 25, has been one of Chelsea’s key players this season and leads the team in several attacking metrics in 2026.

That led to criticism of Rosenior for suspending him for a huge match in Chelsea’s bid to finish in the Champions League places this season.

But the Blues’ boss stuck by his decision, claiming the side will be stronger in the long run because of it.

Rosenior added: “I’ve had three or four really good conversations myself, with Enzo. He’s apologised to me, he’s apologised to the club, and we’ll deal with that after a massive game on Sunday.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“It’s not about individuals, football is a team sport, it’s not about shooting yourself in the foot. There are certain values and cultures that I believe in, that this club believes in, and it makes the team stronger if you get that right.

“Enzo, I’ve said every single step along this way, I’m not questioning his character, I’m not questioning who he is as a person. I believe people make mistakes, and you can’t overstep the punishment for the mistake.

“We made a decision, I made a decision, and what I want for Enzo is for him to come on here and have an outstanding career.”

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior gives Cole Palmer transfer update after dealing with two stars flirting with move
Sports.content:
LIAM ROSENIOR has been working overtime to get the best out of Cole Palmer ahead of the visit of his former club, and reassured fans over his commitment at Stamford Bridge.

Palmer, 23, has struggled this season with various injuries and is enduring his worst season in a Chelsea shirt so far.





The Blues talisman captained the side in their 7-0 win over Port Vale, though, which was their first victory in the last four matches.

And with a tough Premier League run-in, Rosenior, 41, admitted he has been on a quest to find out how to get the best from Palmer in a bid for Champions League qualification next season.

Asked how he can get more out of Palmer, Rosenior said: “You give him confidence. You point out the things he’s doing well. You point out the things that are still very, very positive in his game.

“In terms of chance creation, I’ve gone through the stats. The chances he’s created in our difficult times were very, very high for the league. We just didn’t take the chances that he created. I showed him that.

“You can over-analyse at times, but that’s not what I want Cole to do.

“Cole’s an intuitive player. He needs to be free to express himself to the best of his ability.

“How we have tried to manage Cole before this period is that there were question marks about why he was coming off, why he wasn’t starting games. We wanted him fresh for this period, and so far, he looks really, really good for that.”

In January, SunSport revealed that Palmer would be open to a move away from Chelsea and could be tempted back to Manchester United in the summer window.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And with comments from Enzo Fernandez and Marc Cucurella in recent weeks about potential moves to Spain, Rosenior highlighted Palmer’s commitment to the Blues, including playing through injury at times.

Rosenior added: “I have to give Cole so much credit because he’s put himself up to play for this club, maybe at times where other players wouldn’t.

“A lot of people speak about Cole’s commitment to this club, how much he buys into what we’re doing. He’s fully invested in what we do, in many ways. I’m really, really delighted with him. Just him as a player, as a character, what he stands for, what he wants to achieve.

“He’s going to be a huge part of things for me and the years to come.”



Chelsea, in pursuit of a place in the Premier League top five, have got an extremely difficult run-in.

They face Manchester City on Sunday, before Man Utd visit the following week, with games still to come against Liverpool and Brighton away too.

Their record in games against the ‘big six’, since the club was taken over by BlueCo in 2023, is diabolical and has taken a huge hit.

And to pile on the pessimism of Chelsea fans, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since the 2021 Champions League final, a stretch of 12 matches without a win.
